description: Run Open WebUI (a full Ollama chat interface) in Docker on the remote. It talks to a home-dir Ollama on 127.0.0.1:11434 — the same one the AI Chat plugin uses — so your pulled models appear automatically. If that Ollama isn't running this recipe starts it; if it isn't even installed, it downloads it into ~/.local (no root) so Open WebUI always has a model backend you can pull models into. Uses Docker host networking; HOST=127.0.0.1 keeps Open WebUI on the server's loopback (reached only over the SSH tunnel) — note: with --network=host that loopback bind is enforced by the app honoring HOST, not by Docker. First launch: create an admin account in the browser.

steps.description: Verify Docker is installed (install Docker first if this fails).

Ensure a home-dir Ollama (the same one the AI Chat plugin uses) is running on 127.0.0.1:11434 — start it, or download it into ~/.local with no root if it isn't installed — so Open WebUI always has a model backend and your models appear automatically.
steps.run: set -e; export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"; if ! command -v ollama >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo 'Ollama not found — downloading it into ~/.local (no root)...'; mkdir -p "$HOME/.local"; case "$(uname -m)" in x86_64|amd64) A=amd64 ;; aarch64|arm64) A=arm64 ;; *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac; command -v zstd >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Ollama ships as a .tar.zst archive and needs the 'zstd' tool. Install zstd (e.g. apt-get install zstd) or install the AI Chat plugin first." >&2; exit 1; }; TMP=$(mktemp); curl -fsSL "https://ollama.com/download/ollama-linux-$A.tar.zst" -o "$TMP"; zstd -dc "$TMP" | tar -xf - -C "$HOME/.local"; rm -f "$TMP"; fi; echo 'Starting Ollama on 127.0.0.1:11434...'; export OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11434; mkdir -p "$HOME/.local"; nohup ollama serve >"$HOME/.local/ollama.log" 2>&1 & for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; sleep 1; done; echo 'Ollama did not become ready — Open WebUI will still start; install/run the AI Chat plugin or set the Ollama URL in Open WebUI admin settings.' >&2; tail -n 20 "$HOME/.local/ollama.log" >&2 2>/dev/null || true; exit 1

steps.description: Start the Open WebUI container bound to loopback 127.0.0.1:3000 (host networking → reaches the home-dir Ollama; the loopback bind is enforced by Open WebUI honoring HOST=127.0.0.1, not by Docker). First run pulls a multi-GB image.
steps.run: docker rm -f open-webui 2>/dev/null || true; docker run -d --name open-webui --restart unless-stopped --network=host -e HOST=127.0.0.1 -e PORT=3000 -e ENABLE_OLLAMA_API=true -e OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:11434 -v open-webui:/app/backend/data ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:main

steps.description: Wait for Open WebUI to finish starting (database migrations on first run).
steps.run: for i in $(seq 1 90); do curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:3000/health >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; sleep 2; done; echo 'Open WebUI is still starting — give it a moment, then open it.'

uninstall.description: Stop and remove the Open WebUI container.
Remove the Open WebUI data volume (accounts, chats, settings).
